lines.text: Fall into a small black hole, and you'd turn into spaghetti.

lines.text: Near a small one, gravity pulls your feet harder than your head.

lines.text: You'd stretch long and thin. Scientists really call it spaghettification.

parts.heard: you'd stretch long and thin, scientists really call it spaghettification.

lines.text: But a supermassive black hole, about four million times the Sun's mass, is different.

lines.text: The stretch at its edge is so gentle, you'd cross the point of no return without noticing.

parts.heard: The stretch at its edge is so gentle, you'd cross the point of no return without noticing.

lines.text: But to a friend watching from far away, you'd never quite get there.

lines.text: But inside, every path leads to the center. NASA's simulation says the stretching hits twelve point eight seconds later.
